title: Buckaroo Bowl III
dek: Buckaroo Bowl III, played in NFL week 18 of the 2025 season, ended with Ben Dover (Sonny) beating The fumblers (Randy) 105.1 to 86.48 to claim the first championship in league history not won by Habibsters.
body: Buckaroo Bowl III was the championship game of the 2025 Buckaroo Football League season, the third and final year of the league's original six-team format. It matched the top seed, Ben Dover, managed by Sonny, against the second seed, The fumblers, managed by Randy. Neither manager had won a title before, so the game was guaranteed to produce a first-time champion after Kaushal's Habibsters won Buckaroo Bowls I and II.

Ben Dover entered as the league's dominant regular-season team, finishing 13-3 with 1,850.8 points. The record completed one of the sharpest turnarounds in league history: Sonny had finished last in both 2023 and 2024 with the same team name. The fumblers went 9-7 with 1,792.1 points, a respectable total only 58.7 points behind Ben Dover over the full season.

The two teams met twice in the regular season, and Ben Dover won both comfortably: 118.84 to 88.32 in week 5 and 153.42 to 97.9 in week 10. Despite that history and the gap in the standings, Luffy made The fumblers the favorite, giving Randy a 59 percent chance at the title against 41 percent for Sonny. The forecast set up the game as a contest between the season-long numbers and the win-chance outlook for one specific week.

The fumblers reached the final through a week 17 semifinal against Habibsters, the two-time defending champion. Randy's team won 137.1 to 79.96, a 57.14-point margin that ended Kaushal's bid for a third straight title. Derrick Henry carried the effort with 45.6 points, one of the biggest single-game performances of the 2025 playoffs.

The league's records list no earlier playoff game for Ben Dover in the 2025 postseason. Sonny's team arrived at Buckaroo Bowl III on the strength of its 13-3 regular season and the top seed that came with it, while Randy's side came in off its semifinal rout of the league's dynasty.

Buckaroo Bowl III was a single-week game played over NFL week 18. The site did not record in-game scoring events until week 7 of the 2026 season, so the order in which points arrived during the week is not known. Only final player totals survive.

Ben Dover finished with 105.1 points against The fumblers' 86.48, an 18.6-point margin. Sonny's lineup produced steadily across the roster: four starters scored 14 points or more, and none scored fewer than 5.4. Quarterback Trevor Lawrence led the way with 23.3, and Kenneth Walker III, Justin Jefferson and the Patriots D/ST each beat their projections by a clear margin.

The fumblers' scoring was top-heavy and came from unusual places. The Broncos D/ST (20 points) and kicker Harrison Mevis (15) were two of Randy's three highest scorers, while the skill positions largely failed to deliver. James Cook III and George Pickens, projected for a combined 32.6 points, produced 2.9 between them, and that shortfall decided the game.

For Ben Dover, Trevor Lawrence scored 23.3 points against a 21.5 projection in his first start for the team. Kenneth Walker III scored 15.3 on a 10.6 projection, well above his 9-point average in three earlier starts, and Justin Jefferson added 14.4 against an 11.8 projection and a season average of 9.5. The Patriots D/ST more than doubled its 6.4 projection with 14 points. Sonny's team had soft spots: Trey McBride managed 10 points against a 15.2 season average, George Kittle scored 5.4 in the flex against an 11.8 projection, and Stefon Diggs posted 5.8. None of it mattered, and Sonny's bench offered no improvement, since the Seahawks D/ST (12) and Mike Evans (4.4) would not have outscored the players they could have replaced.

For The fumblers, the Broncos D/ST scored 20 points against a 7.5 projection and a 7.5 average, and Mevis kicked in 15 in his first start for the team. Caleb Williams scored 16.6, slightly below his 19.1 projection and his 17.9 average. The losses came at running back and receiver. James Cook III, a 276-point player who had averaged 18.4 per start, scored 1.5 against a 19.3 projection. George Pickens managed 1.4 against a 13.3 projection and a 15.3 average, and D'Andre Swift produced 5.3 on a 14-point projection.

The decisive lineup question sat on Randy's bench. Amon-Ra St. Brown scored 19.4 points there, beating his 18.1 projection. Starting him over Pickens would have added 18 points and lifted The fumblers to 104.48, still 0.62 short. Deebo Samuel's 3.1 bench points in the flex spot in place of Cook would have added another 1.6, and that combination would have produced 106.08 points, enough to win the championship by 0.98. Randy's starting lineup included three Chicago Bears in Williams, Swift and Luther Burden III, who combined for 27.9 points, while a Detroit Lion sat on the bench and outscored all three of the Bears' skill players.

The victory gave Sonny his first Buckaroo Bowl title and made Ben Dover the first champion other than Habibsters. It completed a worst-to-first arc: a manager who finished last in each of the league's first two seasons won the third with a 13-3 regular season and a two-game sweep of the opponent he would meet in the final. The win also went against Luffy's 59 percent forecast for The fumblers, one of the more notable misses in the forecast's record.

For Randy, the runner-up finish was the best result of his league career to that point, achieved on the back of a semifinal win over the two-time champion. The final, though, is likely to be remembered for the 19.4 points left on the bench and for the two-point combined output of Cook and Pickens.

At the other end of the standings, Mekhi's Dawgs finished last in 2025 through the consolation ladder, taking over a distinction Ben Dover had held for the league's first two seasons. Buckaroo Bowl III was the last championship of the six-team era. The league expanded to eight teams for 2026, when Sonny defended his title under a new team name, The Horse is Hea, and Randy returned with The fumblers.
